title: Chicken drumstick, fried, coated, skin/coating eaten

content.title: About
content.content: A chicken drumstick deep‑fried in a crispy coating is a staple of fast‑food and restaurant menus. Both the skin and the coating are edible, giving the piece a golden color, aromatic flavor, and crunchy texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Deep‑frying is typically done at 175‑190 °C, creating a fast‑forming golden crust.
The coating often contains a blend of flour, spices, and sometimes breadcrumbs, enhancing taste and aroma.
Drumsticks have more connective tissue than breast meat, which helps them stay juicy after frying.
In the United States, breaded fried drumsticks are among the top‑selling items in major fast‑food chains.
They are commonly served with sauces such as barbecue, honey‑mustard, spicy chili, and others.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Chicken meat provides complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Drumsticks are a source of phosphorus, selenium, and zinc, important for bones and immunity.

items.title: Iron
items.content: While lower than red meat, chicken still contributes to maintaining healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fat in the coating helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Deep‑frying and coating increase the dish’s calories and saturated fat levels.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Repeated use of frying oil can generate trans fats, which are harmful to heart health.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Coatings are often salted; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The breading may contain gluten, dairy, or nuts, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Acrylamide
items.content: High‑temperature frying can produce acrylamide, a potential carcinogen.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried drumsticks are usually eaten by hand, dipped in a sauce. They can also be added to salads, placed in a sandwich, or served alongside fries, rice, or vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked drumsticks in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days in an airtight container. For longer storage, freeze them for up to 2 months. Reheat in an oven or air‑fryer to restore crispness.
